narrative.overview: An understated, modern and precise working interface for institutional research. A near-neutral canvas on a faint grid, Geist reading text and compact Geist Mono metadata carry evidence, source references and analyst decisions. Selective glass and one focal surface identify current work without competing with the material being examined.
keyCharacteristics: Near-neutral reading surfaces on a quiet, fading workspace grid.
Geist text and locally hosted Geist Mono metadata.
Selective glass, opaque reading objects and hairline separation.
Analytical meaning conveyed by labels and glyphs as well as tint.
Four workspace destinations and an inventory that opens in context.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Research Violet identifies focus, selection, running work and reasoned-appraisal outcomes; Approval Teal identifies analyst approval, amber identifies pending judgment, and evidence colors identify analytical meaning. Always retain the label and non-color cue.

rules.name: The Shared Type Rule
rules.body: Use sentence case for controls and prose. Reserve uppercase metadata and monospacing for short structural labels, counts and provenance.

rules.name: The Surface Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Use opaque reading regions within selective working surfaces, and separate rows with hairlines. OutcomeCard's dashed outer edges identify unfinished execution; dashed glyphs and frames in other components retain their specific uncertainty meaning, including AppraisalBlock's decisive unknown.

dos: Do keep tokens and variants in their runtime owners and regenerate derived documentation.
Do keep evidence, source membership and analyst judgment visibly distinct.
Do preserve meaningful source controls, keyboard access, loading geometry and direct links.
Do inspect both themes and narrow layouts after shared style changes.
donts: Don't use teal for routine success or evidence colors for unrelated source categories.
Don't fabricate execution, question relationships, appraisal outcomes or change counters.
Don't load the local design export at runtime or maintain a parallel palette.
Don't remove integrity disclosures or substitute a public page for protected workflow verification.
